item.title: Trump says Iran war will end right after US midterm elections
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
US President Donald Trump speaks at the Republican convention in Dallas, US, September 9, 2026. /VCG
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the war with Iran will end "immediately after" the US midterm elections in November, arguing that Tehran would not be able to withstand continued US economic pressure as fighting escalated sharply around the Strait of Hormuz.
His remarks came as the conflict entered its seventh month, with renewed clashes near the Strait of Hormuz pushing oil prices higher. Benchmark Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel for the first time since July.
Trump said oil prices would also fall after the war ends, while acknowledging that negotiations remain possible, though he said they were not his preferred option. The midterm elections, scheduled for November 3, are widely viewed as a key political test for the president, whose approval ratings have been hit by voter concerns over the Iran war and rising living costs.
Trump’s prediction contrasted with warnings reportedly delivered by some of his senior advisers, who privately told him the conflict could continue through the remainder of his presidency, according to The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials.
The report said Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were among officials who warned that Tehran could continue resisting US pressure, potentially prolonging the conflict beyond January 2029. The White House did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
The latest escalation followed a series of attacks involving vessels near the Strait of Hormuz. The US military said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers after an Iranian attack on a US warship, while Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had carried out retaliatory strikes against two US warships and eight US oil tankers. The US Central Command denied that its naval ships had been attacked.
Iran’s Foreign Ministry condemned the US strikes, saying Iranian forces had carried out what it described as defensive strikes against US military facilities and vessels and would respond to what it called military aggression.
The confrontation has affected shipping activity in the region, with preliminary data from ship-tracking firm Kpler showing that only six commercial vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, below both the previous day’s level and the recent average.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said Tehran had the capability to retaliate against any attacks and warned that Iran would respond with broader strikes if targeted. He also outlined conditions for ending the conflict, including a halt to military operations, an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, the lifting of the blockade on Yemen, the release of frozen Iranian assets and an end to pressure on Iran’s nuclear and missile programs.
Mohebbi also said Iran would establish a new maritime "sanctions zone," where vessels entering the area would face restrictions on maritime services and insurance.

item.title: China services trade fair showcases innovation, promotes openness
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) opened Wednesday in Beijing, as China steps up efforts to expand opening-up in services trade at the outset of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030).
Running through Sept. 13 at Shougang Park, a former industrial site and venue for the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics, the fair has drawn participants from 90 countries, regions and international organizations, with over 1,800 companies exhibiting on-site. Among them are 473 Fortune Global 500 firms and other industry leaders, including Honeywell, Johnson & Johnson and Siemens.
Themed "Global Services, Shared Prosperity," this year's CIFTIS features a Global Trade in Services Summit, co-hosted by China's Ministry of Commerce and the Beijing municipal government, together with the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO). A series of forums and business matchmaking activities will also be held during the fair.
During the summit, Zimbabwean Vice President Constantino Chiwenga said the CIFTIS is expected to create many investment opportunities across conferencing, exhibition, infrastructure, and digital services, adding that it will help Zimbabwe identify opportunities for trade in services, build export capacity, and attract credible partners across technology, finance, tourism, education and health care.
Alexander Poulev, deputy prime minister and minister of Economy, Investment and Industry of Bulgaria, said at the summit that trade in services is an important pillar of the China-Bulgarian relationship. "We want to see more Bulgarian products reaching the Chinese market and more Bulgarian companies building long-term partnerships with Chinese businesses," he said.
More than 100 new products and services will make their debut at the fair, covering fields such as information and communications, fintech, and digital and intelligent healthcare.
Another highlight is a new overseas expansion services roadshow area, which offers Chinese companies one-stop professional support to enter foreign markets and expand the global footprint of Chinese services.
"Going global today is no longer just about competitive pricing, but also about adapting to different rules, managing compliance and navigating risks," said Li Yao from KPMG China, adding that the new service area comes at an opportune time.
The core exhibition area also debuts a showcase of more than 140 innovation cases spanning all 12 categories of services trade, including artificial intelligence, large language models, and intelligent agents, offering a glimpse of where China's services sector is headed.
Advancing trade in services and promoting opening up and cooperation in the services sector is not only China's choice but also a global necessity, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang said in a keynote speech at the summit. He noted China's efforts in actively promoting trade in services and opening up its services sector wider, which are creating more opportunities for countries and businesses around the world.
The fair itself offered a glimpse of that openness in action. Norway, this year's guest country of honor, presented a pavilion featuring a wide range of exhibits, including health and nutrition, green transition, and design and lifestyle.
Henning Kristoffersen, commercial counselor of the Norwegian Embassy in Beijing, said the opportunity allows Norway to show a much broader picture of its commercial relationship with China. "What we want to do at CIFTIS is to broaden it further into services, technology, culture and knowledge-based cooperation," he said. China is Norway's largest trading partner in Asia, with around 160 Norwegian companies operating in China, he added.
Klaus Hoseth, CEO of Hoseth Technology, a Norwegian fish-processing technology firm, is attending CIFTIS for the first time and looking to cooperate with Chinese robotics and AI companies. "We hope to improve automation and efficiency in our production line, and leverage Chinese open-source AI technologies to make factory systems smarter," he said. He also noted the strong potential for cooperation between China's vast market and Norway's marine food industry.
The interest shown by international participants comes as China's services trade continues to grow.
China has posted rapid growth in services trade, with strong exports of knowledge-intensive services supported by the country's IP and innovation ecosystem, said WIPO Director General Daren Tang in his video address to the summit.
Latest official data showed that in the first seven months of 2026, China's services trade totaled nearly 4.45 trillion yuan (about 656.6 billion U.S. dollars), up 8.3 percent year on year.
A report released at CIFTIS on Wednesday also highlighted the growing strength of China's services brands. China ranks second globally with 21 brands in the world's 100 most valuable trade in services brands, with a combined worth of 876.8 billion U.S. dollars, according to the report titled "Trade in Services 100 2026" released by Brand Finance, a leading brand valuation consultancy.
Advancing high-quality development of services trade is a key task in the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), which calls for intensified efforts to optimize negative list management of services trade, ease cross-border restrictions, encourage services exports, and foster knowledge-intensive services trade.

item.title: China recognizes 11 new occupations as new industries create fresh roles
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
A staff member trains a humanoid robot to sort and arrange yarn tubes at a humanoid robot training facility in Cixi City, east China's Zhejiang Province, Sept. 3, 2026.(Xinhua/Xu Yu)
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China on Wednesday officially recognized 11 new occupations and 23 new specialties under existing occupations, reflecting evolving labor demand driven by technological advances, industrial upgrading and shifting consumer needs.
The new occupations, released by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and other government departments, include shore-based ship management engineering technicians, embodied intelligence robot technicians and sports data analysts.
Authorities also revised information concerning six existing occupations or specialties, including agricultural product brokers.
The recognition of the new occupations and specialties will help promote employment and entrepreneurship, offer workers more diverse career paths and better match talent supply with job demand.
Five of the newly recognized occupations are classified as digital occupations and three as green occupations, bringing the respective totals in China to 113 and 142.
A ministry official said China is expected to face a sizable shortage of workers with digital skills for some time, adding that the recognition of the new occupations would spur training and open up broad employment prospects.
The latest additions also highlight the continued expansion of modern services.
Some of these new occupations focus on business development and industrial upgrading, including corporate sustainability planners, airport obstacle-clearance inspectors, and artificial intelligence (AI) agent developers. Others respond more directly to people's demand for higher-quality services, including incense-making artisans, smart furniture assembly and commissioning workers, and fresh-cut flower processing workers.
More modern service occupations are expected to emerge amid the increasing specialization and upgrading of producer services and improvements in the quality, diversity and convenience of consumer services, the official said.
New specialties under existing occupations include community workers, low-altitude logistics operators and age-friendly renovation designers.
Since 2019, China has released eight batches of 121 new occupations.
Of these new occupations, 60 percent were service-related, while professional and technical occupations and manufacturing-related occupations each accounted for 17 percent.
By industry, 43 percent of the new occupations were in modern services, while 34 percent were in advanced manufacturing.
The ministry said it will formulate national standards for the new occupations to guide vocational education, skills training and talent assessment.
During the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period, China aims to explore new employment space in the digital economy, green economy and silver economy.

item.title: China firmly opposes U.S. groundless allegations on Chinese AI firms: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Commerce on Wednesday voiced firm opposition to the recent U.S. announcements that Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) companies are engaged in so-called industrial-scale efforts to distill capabilities from U.S. AI models, calling the accusations groundless and without legal basis.
The U.S. move politicizes distillation, which is a normal technical and commercial issue in the AI industry, a ministry spokesperson said, adding the U.S. announcements are another proof of the country's pursuit of technological hegemony and computing power monopoly in the AI field, as well as its suppression of competition.
Distillation is a common practice for mutual learning among AI models, which is essentially a neutral technical means used by global model companies including U.S. firms. It can help models enhance their learning efficiency, achieve more efficient utilization of human knowledge, and is significant for the development of the AI industry in various countries.
China's open-source models are open to global enterprises, including those from the United States. Some U.S. enterprises have disclosed the distillation of a large number of Chinese models, the spokesperson said.
However, the U.S. side has repeatedly and unilaterally accused Chinese enterprises of engaging in "industrial-scale" distillation, and smeared common practices as aggressive acts. This reflects the anxiety and double standards of the United States, the spokesperson said.
The United States frequently threatened sanctions on and suppression of Chinese companies' distillation practices this year, aiming to maintain the U.S. monopoly in computing power and data, and prevent other countries from participating in the inclusive sharing of AI innovation achievements, the spokesperson said.
China and the United States should handle the challenges and risks in the AI field in a proactive and responsible manner. The two heads of state have agreed to hold an inter-governmental dialogue on AI. China is willing to engage in constructive and professional discussions with the United States based on the principles of equality, mutual benefit and win-win cooperation, said the spokesperson.
If the U.S. side takes actions to suppress Chinese AI enterprises under the pretext of targeting distillation, China will surely take resolute countermeasures, the spokesperson added.

item.title: How China drives BRICS expansion and cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Delhi Police personnel stand guard at Pragati Maidan ahead of the upcoming BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, September 6, 2026. /VCG
At the 18th BRICS Summit to be held in New Delhi, India, this upcoming weekend, BRICS has taken on a new meaning. The summit’s theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability," also abbreviated as BRICS, highlights the priorities of the organization's new phase of development.
From five countries to 11 members, and from a small group of emerging economies to a platform representing half of the world's population, BRICS has come a long way.
Accounting for 40% of global GDP and with intra-BRICS trade reaching $1.17 trillion in 2024, BRICS has gained considerable weight as it evolves into an increasingly important force in global economics and governance.
China's contribution to BRICS expansion
China has been at the heart of this evolution, especially in promoting inclusiveness and cooperation in BRICS.
At the 2017 Xiamen Summit, China first put forward the "BRICS plus" model, seeking to expand BRICS cooperation to a wider range of emerging economies and amplify the voice of the Global South. Inviting leaders from Egypt, Guinea, Mexico, Tajikistan and Thailand to the summit during its chairmanship, China took the lead in building an open and diversified network of partnerships to boost cooperation on a broader scale.
That proposal soon translated into the membership expansion process. Since then, six new countries, including Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates, have become full members of the organization, culminating in the "Greater BRICS" and a new phase of development that features an enlarged circle of friends.
Following through with its proposal, China has consistently supported BRICS expansion throughout the years. In 2024, BRICS formally established the partner country mechanism, creating a pathway for countries to engage more closely with the bloc without immediately becoming full members. Reaffirming its commitment to an open and inclusive BRICS, China has continued to support more countries in joining the BRICS mechanism, pool the strength of the Global South and build a shared future.
Through its expansion, BRICS will not only help strengthen solidarity and cooperation among developing countries but also enable them to jointly address global economic risks and achieve more stable development, according to a study by Xi Manzhao, a teaching assistant at the School of Northeast Asian Studies, Shandong University, and Yang Yanlong, a research fellow at the Institute of International Studies, Shandong University.
China's solution to global challenges
BRICS's growth is made meaningful through practical measures. To this end, China has also proposed original solutions to common global challenges.
For instance, China has led the establishment of multiple collaborative centers. The China-BRICS Artificial Intelligence Development and Cooperation Center aims to make AI more accessible and affordable for businesses and local governments to solve real, local problems. The BRICS Deep-Sea Resources International Research Center pools research strengths from BRICS nations to tackle resource scarcity and promote equitable, sustainable ocean development. Meanwhile, the China Center for Cooperation on Development of Special Economic Zones in BRICS Countries boosts trade collaboration, policy exchange, and institutional innovation among BRICS nations and emerging markets.
China's contribution not only establishes practical cooperation platforms but also sets up financial mechanisms.
As a founding member of the New Development Bank (NDB), China helped establish a multilateral development bank that provides financing for infrastructure and sustainable development projects. China also pushed for consensus on the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA), which offers mutual liquidity support and protection from short-term payment pressures, according to a United Nations Trade and Development report.
As BRICS enters a new era with more members and opportunities, China has helped turn the bloc's vision into concrete platforms and mechanisms to address shared development challenges.
Ezzat Saad El Sayed, director of the Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs, highlighted China's vital role at the 2025 BRICS summit.
"We cannot imagine what BRICS would look like without China,” he said. “China is a major pillar and a powerful driving force behind BRICS cooperation."

item.title: China's inflation edges up, signaling sustained recovery in domestic demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Customers buy goods at a supermarket in Liangyuan District of Shangqiu, central China's Henan Province, Sept. 9, 2026. Data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Wednesday showed the consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4 percent month on month in August, reversing three consecutive months of decline, while the year-on-year gain accelerated from 0.5 percent to 0.8 percent. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy prices, edged up to 1 percent year on year from 0.9 percent the previous month. (Photo by Li Heng/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's price levels continued their moderate recovery in August, reflecting sustained improvement in domestic demand under supportive policy measures.
NBS statistician Dong Lijuan attributed the uptick to several factors: rising energy prices, seasonal increases in food prices, continued gains in travel services during the summer holiday period, and higher prices for smartphones and computers driven by the surging demand for computing power.
Factory-gate prices also sent encouraging signals. The producer price index (PPI) rose 0.4 percent month on month in August, swinging from a 0.7 percent decline the previous month, while the year-on-year gain widened to 3.8 percent.
The NBS cited the pass-through effect of rising global commodity prices and stronger demand in some sectors driven by domestic industrial upgrading.
Wednesday's price data is consistent with the broad pickup in consumer activity seen across China this summer.
Railway passenger trips totaled 954 million in July and August combined, and summer box office receipts reached 12.5 billion yuan (1.84 billion U.S. dollars). To channel consumer enthusiasm, more than 30,000 events centered on summer leisure, study tours and night economy were held nationwide, while over 450 million yuan in consumption subsidies were distributed by local governments.
Expanding domestic demand remains high on China's economic agenda. At a high-level meeting in late July, policymakers called for effectively expanding domestic demand, broadening quality supply to meet the needs of different consumer groups, and tapping the potential of service consumption. The Ministry of Commerce recently issued a set of guidelines to accelerate the release of demand for personalized consumption.
Experts believe more efforts should be made to smooth the flow of consumption and lift income expectations of individuals.
Chasing Securities predicts the policy measures to continue driving a moderate recovery in price levels. Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Golden Credit Rating, forecasts that CPI will continue to edge up year on year in September, with price levels expected to remain moderate.
The role of consumption as a primary engine of economic growth is set to strengthen. Official data showed final consumption expenditure contributed 2.1 percentage points to GDP growth in the first half of the year, continuing to lead all growth drivers.
For the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China has released a dedicated consumption expansion plan setting out 28 priority measures, with efforts to cultivate new consumption models and scenarios, raise household spending capacity, and optimize the consumer environment.
A strong domestic demand helps ensure a stable economy. With expanding domestic demand as a strategic anchor, China's pro-consumption policies will inject sustained internal growth momentum into the broader economy, experts said.

item.title: Xi's Central Asia, Middle East tour injects certainty, positive energy into world in flux
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Chinese President Xi Jinping attends a group photo session during a welcome banquet held by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov ahead of the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus" meeting in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Sept. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye)
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping made a five-day trip to Central Asia and the Middle East from Aug. 30 to Sept. 3, during which he attended the 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit and paid state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt, sending strong messages that inject certainty and positive energy into a turbulent and changing world.
The trip, observers say, was in step with the broader trends of the times as the Chinese president, with the shared future of humanity in mind, advanced a series of proposals on reforming and improving global governance.
VISION FOR AN "EQUAL AND ORDERLY MULTIPOLAR WORLD"
At the expanded SCO Plus Meeting in Bishkek, capital of Kyrgyzstan, Xi called for an "equal and orderly multipolar world" and a more just and equitable global governance system, with a stronger role for the United Nations.
The SCO, since its establishment in 2001, has grown from a six-member Eurasian organization to a 27-nation family across Asia, Europe and Africa.
In his speech, Xi said that sovereign equality and mutual respect are fundamental principles; balance, order and the rule of law are inherent requirements; multilateralism, dialogue and consultation are essential pathways; and mutual benefit, win-win, and inclusiveness are the way forward for development.
These principles are rooted in Xi's vision for global governance, first articulated with the launch of the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) at last year's SCO Summit in China's coastal city of Tianjin, as the United Nations marked its 80th anniversary.
The initiative has received support from nearly 160 countries and international organizations. The Group of Friends of Global Governance has been established in New York, Geneva and Vienna. The World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, the world's first intergovernmental international organization on AI, has been launched in Shanghai for AI governance. These efforts help turn the GGI into concrete actions.
Put forward by Xi, the Global Governance Initiative, along with the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, and the Global Civilization Initiative, has been widely acclaimed, said SCO Secretary-General Nurlan Yermekbayev.
"This is a complementary system of ideas and practical approaches aimed at addressing pressing contemporary challenges and building a just, peaceful, and sustainable world order," he said.
During this trip, the Chinese president sought to promote peace, development and prosperity in both international and regional arenas.
At SCO meetings, Xi outlined four proposals for advancing the organization's high-quality development and three suggestions for enhancing its role.
During his state visit to Kyrgyzstan, Xi signed a bilateral treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation with his Kyrgyz counterpart.
In Egypt, Xi proposed a four-point approach to building a new Middle East security architecture.
DEVELOPMENT FOR THE PEOPLE
In his talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov, Xi called for efforts to advance the building of a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future and better benefit the people of both countries.
He urged high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, a flagship Belt and Road project linking China with Central Asia.
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and his wife Aigul Japarova in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)
Addressing the SCO summit, Xi called on the SCO to put development first and open up the prospects for shared prosperity.
The SCO, Xi said, should champion a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, consolidate cooperation in traditional areas such as trade and investment, connectivity, energy and resources, and expand cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, digital economy, green industry and green mining.
The same emphasis on development and people's wellbeing was evident during Xi's visit to Egypt. In a joint communique, China praised Egypt's Decent Life Initiative for its efforts to improve people's living standards, while Egypt expressed appreciation for the Global Development Initiative.
As Xi once put it, "People's sense of gain should be the goal of domestic governance and global governance, and we should continue to provide confidence and stable expectations for the people."
MUTUAL LEARNING
In a signed article published ahead of his visit to Kyrgyzstan, Xi wrote about the ancient Silk Road as a witness to the long-standing friendship between the two peoples, citing the stories of historical figures such as diplomat Zhang Qian, monk Xuanzang and poet Li Bai, whose legacy is seen as promoting civilizational exchanges between China and Kyrgyzstan.
During his visit to Egypt, Xi, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, visited the Grand Egyptian Museum, where the legacy of ancient Egypt unfolds against the backdrop of the millennia-old pyramids.
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi, tour the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
Xi and Sisi, together with their spouses, spent more than one hour touring the museum, home to more than 100,000 precious artifacts.
They toured the grand galleries, posing for a photo before a towering statue of Ramses II, one of the most famous pharaohs of Egypt, as curators delivered a swift primer on pharaonic history.
"This museum is a book with endless pages," Xi said.
The museum visit also underscored Xi's longstanding emphasis on exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations.
Over the years, Xi's overseas trips have taken him to museums and historic sites, from the Amir Timur Museum in Uzbekistan to the ancient Maya ruins of Chichen Itza in Mexico. At home, he also invited foreign leaders to visit China's historic sites, ranging from the Forbidden City to the ancient irrigation system Dujiangyan and the over 600-year-old Temple of Heaven.
At the Grand Egyptian Museum, Xi called on the two countries to promote inclusive coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, and pool greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity.
The remarks echoed Xi's message to Sisi on the museum's opening last year, in which Xi highlighted the vibrant cultural and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, citing the successful exhibition on ancient Egyptian civilization in Shanghai and joint archaeological exploration into the pyramids at Saqqara, located south of Cairo.
"It is encouraging to see the two ancient civilizations reaching out to each other, with the two peoples growing ever closer through mutual understanding and affinity," Xi said.

item.title: Pushing in by Land, Water and Air: Expert Explains Extreme Hurdles in Mudslide Rescue
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
A total of 2,141 rescue personnel have been mobilized for search and rescue operations after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. Rescue teams are advancing into the hardest-hit core area simultaneously by water, land and air. An expert explained mudslides like this occur under particular terrain and water conditions, and that creates several challenges for rescue teams.
